name: Ramp
text: Implement skip links to allow users to bypass repetitive content and navigation. This enhances keyboard usability and improves navigation for those using assistive technologies, aligning with our goal of making EXCAVA accessible for everyone. The trade-off is that it may require additional design considerations to ensure visibility and usability, but the increase in accessibility benefits outweighs the complexity.

name: Reader
text: Skip links alone don’t solve the core problem—they’re just a bandage over missing landmarks and keyboard traps. The real risk is users still hit dead ends if the page structure lacks proper headings, focus order, or interactive controls. Test with a keyboard-only user: if they can’t reach every critical action, skip links won’t save them. Settle it by auditing the full focus path and fixing traps first—then add skip links as a refinement.

name: Ramp

We should prioritize establishing a clear heading structure throughout EXCAVA to enhance navigation for keyboard users and assistive technologies. This decision directly addresses the core accessibility issues by providing logical landmarks that users can easily navigate. The trade-off is that it may require a comprehensive audit of existing content and potentially reorganizing sections, but this foundational change will create a more intuitive experience and reduce user frustration.

name: Reader
text: Headings alone won’t fix keyboard traps or missing interactive controls—users will still get stuck if focus order is broken or critical elements aren’t reachable. The real fix is auditing the entire page flow with a keyboard-only user, then enforcing focus order and interactive control visibility as the priority. Settle it by running a live test: if a keyboard user can’t complete a core task (like submitting a form), the structure is still broken.
